title: When recursion never stops
summary: What StackOverflowError means and how to fix it.

say.never: This version forgot to stop. With no base case, `factorial(3)` calls `factorial(2)`, then `factorial(1)`, then 0, then -1, then -2, and so on forever. Each call waits in memory for the next, until Java runs out of room and stops with a **StackOverflowError**.
say.bit: This version forgot to stop at 0, so it keeps calling `factorial(-1)`, `factorial(-2)`... forever.

board.caption: Exception: java.lang.StackOverflowError

say.never: The fix has two rules. Every path must reach a base case, so there's a place to stop. And every call must move *toward* it, so you actually get there. Here, `n - 1` moves toward 1, and `n <= 1` is where it stops.
say.bit: Every path must reach a base case, and every step must move **toward** it.

say.never: Strings work the same way. `reverseString` makes the text shorter on every call: take the last letter, then add the reverse of everything before it. When the text is empty or has one letter, there's nothing left to reverse, and that's the base case.
say.bit: `reverseString` shrinks the string each call: the last character, plus the reverse of everything before it, until it's 0 or 1 characters long.
